title: Alejandro Garnacho and the curious case of Aston Villa’s outcast loanees | Ben Fisher
summary: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

title: Champions League: Lille comeback adds to Bayern woes, Gordon leads Barcelona rout
summary: Lille 2-1 Bayern Munich, Sabah 1-4 Barcelona Malen penalty earns Roma 2-2 draw at PSG Bayern Munich endured their first defeat of the season on Wednesday, losing 2-1 at Lille in the Champions League as a tough week for the German giants worsened. Dayot Upamecano opened the scoring for Bayern but Ayase Ueda levelled for Lille before a horror Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal gifted the hosts victory. Bayern’s unbeaten record in all competitions was ended by a Lille side who kicked off in 35th place in the tournament’s league phase. Continue reading...

title: Isak and Wirtz on target as resurgent Liverpool sweep aside Club Brugge
summary: Liverpool, from big money individuals to the collective, are building formidable momentum. On a bitterly cold night in Belgium, Andoni Iraola’s team delivered an accomplished away display to bring Club Brugge’s impressive run to a halt and step closer to automatic qualification from the Champions League group. A week that supposedly represented a test of Liverpool’s credentials has brought rich encouragement before Sunday’s Merseyside derby. Following the 4-0 destruction of Manchester United there was another display of outstanding finishing from Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz. Continue reading...

title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
summary: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

title: Has a footballer had a longer career hiatus than Ronaldinho’s 11 year-gap? | The Knowledge
summary: Plus: the quickest team to go from FA Cup winners to the first round and matches delayed by snowball fights Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Ronaldinho played for Ravenna, in Serie C, earlier this month. It was his first professional appearance in more than 11 years,” writes George Jones. “Have any other footballers had long career hiatuses? And has any player had a longer hiatus than 11 years?” Ronaldinho’s last professional appearance before his return for Ravenna came on 26 September 2015 for Fluminense, who won 2-0 at home against Goiás. He was withdrawn after 45 minutes. Fans of symmetry will be pleased to see that 11 years and 50 days later, the Brazilian returned for Ravenna in a 2-0 home win against another team with five letters and an accent in their name, Forlì, and was withdrawn after 45 minutes. Continue reading...

title: ‘He’s more elegant’: Bellingham downplays Zidane comparisons after wondergoal
summary: Englishman hailed by teammates and manager Mourinho after coming on to completely change Champions League game against PSV Eindhoven “It was one of those moments when you’re just: ‘Wow.’” Bernardo Silva had a good view of Jude Bellingham scoring the goal, the golazo , that put Real Madrid into the lead and the Bernabéu on its feet, shock giving way to song, naa, naa, naa, na-na-na-naa, na-na-na-naa ringing round again. “I have no idea what I did,” the Englishman said afterwards. What he did was turn all Le Tissier. Lifting the ball with his left, raising it with his right, twisting and not letting it drop, he sent it arching from the outside of his boot into the far corner, something straight out of the 90s. “I just kind of hit it,” Bellingham reckoned; not wanting to hit it too hard, it had gone “looping”, “stabbing”, he said. “Normally [my goals are] a lot closer, aren’t they? I was a bit surprised, honestly. Normally from there I’m looking to see who is an option to play it through to, but it popped up nicely. It was nice.” Nice? It was, Silva said, “special”. A “work of art” Marca called it. The presenter on one radio station claimed it was the best goal he had ever seen, and it wasn’t just him; wasn’t just the goal, either. Continue reading...

title: Football Daily | Manchester City get that empty feeling as they fail to win again
summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Early in the second half of Tuesday night’s National League South match between Torquay United and Chesham, play was briefly suspended due to an ear-splitting din emitted over the Plainmoor public address system. “The game has stopped because the Torquay Tannoy system is making a loud noise that won’t stop,” posted Chesham on their Social Media Disgrace account. “I’m not kidding.” A sort of aural cross between an ocean liner’s foghorn and a party conference speech delivered by a senior member of the Reform party, it eventually stopped and play resumed with Torquay running out 2-1 winners. In this constantly changing world of global disruptions, uncertainties and risks, with social, political and economic disaffection seemingly on the rise everywhere, it’s genuinely heartening to know that some things never change . ‘Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose’, as the late, great French writer Jean-Baptiste Alphonse Karr famously said, something that I’m sure Big Dunc is well aware of” – Noble Francis. May I be the 1,092nd correspondent to demand a review of the Letter o’ the Day award for Monday – and it be awarded to Declan Hackett for his letter foretelling the rescinding of the red card given to Lenny Yoro on Sunday? Given the precedent of awarding/revoking/re-awarding of the Afcon 2025 edition this would be entirely justified” – Peter Martin. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

title: Oliver Glasner criticises Nottingham Forest players for not learning English
summary: ‘Players are here for four years and can’t speak English’ Glasner has held talks with owner over January moves Nottingham Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, believes standards at the club were not good enough prior to his arrival as he questioned why some of his squad cannot speak English after a number of years in the country. Glasner was tempted to move to the City Ground by owner Evangelos Marinakis after winning the FA Cup and Conference League at Crystal Palace. However, Forest have won two of their opening 11 Premier League games and sit outside the relegation zone only on goal difference. Continue reading...

title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
summary: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, not long after the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to the finals of the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentine Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
summary: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

title: Raheem Sterling avoids jail over reckless driving while using nitrous oxide
summary: He gets 12-month sentence suspended for 18 months Former England forward must do community service Raheem Sterling has avoided being sent to jail after he received a suspended sentence of 12 months for pleading guilty to a prolonged period of reckless driving while impaired by the drug nitrous oxide. The former England international, who five years ago was leading the Three Lions’ charge to a European Championship final, stood expressionless in the dock as the sentence was read out by district judge Kirsty Allman at Basingstoke magistrates court. Continue reading...

title: Saudi Arabia’s PIF looking to sell 25% of Newcastle through share issue
summary: PIF seeking investment to fund infrastructure projects JP Morgan appointed to handle the sale Newcastle United’s owner, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), is looking to sell up to 25% of the club by issuing new shares. The New York-based bank JP Morgan, whose most recent involvement in a major football deal was Fifa’s aborted attempt to sell off 20% of its commercial rights last summer, has been appointed to handle the sale, as first reported by the Athletic . title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to fiasco but issues do not stop there | Osasu Obayiuwana
summary: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. Continue reading...

title: ‘I have 100 witnesses’: the 10 wildest moments from Aaron Rodgers’ explosive ESPN interview
summary: From a half-time huddle gone wrong to an ultimatum over play-calling, here’s what the quarterback said Wednesday in a scorched-earth appearance on Pat McAfee’s show Barely 12 hours after the Pittsburgh Steelers announced that Aaron Rodgers would be deactivated and Mason Rudolph would start Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player left no bridge unburned in a surprise call-in to ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show. In a 34-minute appearance on Wednesday afternoon where he spoke uninterrupted for long stretches, Rodgers accused Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep in a quarterback meeting, skipping walkthroughs and falling behind on film study. He also said the 63-year-old McCarthy broke a half-time huddle against Philadelphia with the words “One, two, three, Packers”. According to Rodgers, McCarthy denied falling asleep at the team facility. Continue reading...

title: Steelers release Aaron Rodgers after he accuses Mike McCarthy of sleeping during meetings
summary: Quarterback was benched by team this week Rodgers had said he would retire after season The Pittsburgh Steelers released Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday, hours after the four-time NFL MVP accused head coach Mike McCarthy of falling asleep during team meetings. Rodgers made the sensational allegations during a surprise 34-minute appearance on ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show after the Steelers benched him in favor of backup quarterback Mason Rudolph. Continue reading...

title: Greg Fisilau to make England debut start in blockbuster All Blacks rematch
summary: Borthwick makes five changes for New Zealand game Head coach says he likes Pollock’s impact off the bench Steve Borthwick has admitted he considers Henry Pollock most dangerous in his role of supersub after again leaving him on the bench against New Zealand and instead handing Greg Fisilau a surprise first start. The 23-year-old Fisilau came into the autumn uncapped but has impressed off the bench in all three of England’s victories and is rewarded with his first start as Borthwick’s side bid for a third straight win over New Zealand for the first time. title: Gukesh and Sindarov draw Game 2 of world chess championship in just 20 moves
summary: Game 2 ends by threefold repetition in 1hr 57min World champion opens with the London System Sindarov plays with white in Game 3 on Thursday All your Gukesh v Sindarov questions, answered India’s Gukesh Dommaraju and Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov drew the second game of their world chess championship match in only 20 moves and 1hr 57min on Wednesday, leaving the score level at 1–all at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the Geneva suburbs. The quiet encounter was one of the shortest classical world title games since the sport’s rival championships were reunified in 2006 and the first to finish in under two hours since Ding Liren and Ian Nepomniachtchi drew their 11th game in just over 100 minutes in Astana in 2023. Continue reading...

title: London Broncos’ promotion and 15-team Super League confirmed for 2027 season
summary: Top-flight clubs and Rugby Football League strike deal Co-owner: ‘We have tremendous momentum on the field’ London Broncos’ promotion to Super League for the 2027 season has been confirmed following an agreement between the existing top-flight clubs and the Rugby Football League. Broncos won all but one of their 24 matches in the second-tier Championship last season, scoring 1,511 points, but failed to earn enough points in the sport’s IMG gradings system to secure automatic elevation. title: MLB sues players’ association in order to ensure lockout is declared legal
summary: League looks to head off antitrust threat by MLBPA Lockout a looming likelihood due to salary cap dispute MLB sued its players’ association in federal court on Wednesday, asking that its likely lockout next week be declared legal and trying to head off any attempt by the union to decertify and challenge the work stoppage with an antitrust case. In a 38-page complaint filed in US District Court in Manhattan, MLB and the corporate entities owning its 30 teams sued the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) and the eight players on the union’s executive subcommittee, including record-setting pitcher Tarik Skubal. Continue reading...

title: The Spin | South Africa fans are furious over tickets for New Year Test, but are they right to be?
summary: Series against England promises packed stands but home fans have accused Cricket South Africa of prioritising wealthy tourists In the afterglow of South Africa’s nine-wicket victory against Bangladesh at the Wanderers last week, Kagiso Rabada admitted that the occasion had been unusually difficult. Strange, considering he had claimed eight wickets and struck a career-best 72 in a player-of-the-match performance. But the opposition wasn’t the problem. His struggle was with the empty stands, which made an international Test feel more “like a domestic fixture” than the pinnacle of the sport. This is an extract from the Guardian’s weekly cricket email, The Spin. To subscribe, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

title: ‘It’s stressful but better than having a proper job’: the life of a cricket umpire
summary: Four umpires discuss how they deal with players, why they avoid social media, how technology is changing cricket and why umpiring beats being a football referee By Wisden Cricket Monthly Last summer, sat in a quiet ground at the fag-end of a four-dayer, with a few souls still kicking around and a clutch of cameras streaming what was left of the day live on YouTube, it struck me again what a great, strange sanctuary this place is, out there on the edges of the modern world. The game is trying to move, albeit at its own pace. Later that night, the day’s highlights would be landing on social media, available to all, for the game’s devotees to pore over and pick apart. More people are watching the County Championship than ever before. Streaming numbers show a growing audience in the UK and a widening uptake across the cricketing globe. The numbers aren’t yet earth-shattering, but how could they be, with such eccentric fare? Continue reading...

title: Twickenham confident pitch can take six games in three days for Nations Championship
summary: Groundsman on 15-hour days across finals weekend England in home dressing room against All Blacks The Rugby Football Union’s head groundsman is confident Twickenham’s pitch will hold up to staging six matches across three days for the Nations Championship finals, detailing the lengths to which he and his support staff will go. In preparation for the showpiece weekend, the turf – which had been in place since 2012 – was ripped up over the summer with a new state-of-the-art hybrid surface laid. It comes complete with a reservoir that can hold 1.4m litres of water below it – which can be reused using nanobubble technology – and was grown in Scunthorpe before being transported to south-west London. Continue reading...

title: Kurtley Beale ends five-year exile as Allan Alaalatoa joins Wallabies’ 100 club
summary: 37-year-old Beale on bench for final Nations Championship game Prop Alaalatoa to co-captain side in landmark appearance Kurtley Beale’s five-year exile from international rugby is set to end after the veteran playmaker was named on the bench for Australia’s season-ending clash with Ireland at Twickenham. Beale last represented the Wallabies against Wales in Cardiff in 2021 but the 37-year-old is among the replacements as Australia look to build on last week’s dramatic 29-26 win over Wales – a result that ended a run of four straight defeats.
